newsitem.title: FRANCE: Credit National dips to first-half loss.
newsitem.headline: Credit National dips to first-half loss.

text.p: French bank Credit National said on Wednesday it fell into loss in the first half of 1996 due to provisions of 250 million francs for restructuring in the wake of buying the Banque Francaise de Commerce Exterieur (BFCE).

Chairman Emmanuel Rodocanachi said the second six months of the year would be better now that the provisions had been taken care of and that the bank's aim was to get back above breakeven for the year as a whole.
Rodocanachi announced a first-half net attributable loss of 112 million francs, versus a profit of 267 million francs for the same period a year earlier.
The 1995 figure was restated to account for the integration of the previously state-owned trade finance bank BFCE.

Net banking income also slid to 1.98 billion francs from 2.09 billion francs. Rodocanachi said there had been weaker credit demand from its main client base of medium and large companies and increased margin pressure.
One provision for a failure on the capital investment side of the bank's operations had also taken its toll, he told a news conference without elaborating.

Credit National's share slid on the Paris stock exchange in morning trading to a year low of 283 francs before recovering slightly to 286.8 francs, down 22.5 francs, by 1044 GMT against the trend in the CAC 40 leading share index.

The company said in its statement it was talking to employee representatives about cost cuts because staffing levels were likely to represent an "excess equivalent to 600 full-time jobs" by 1998, due largely to overlap after the BFCE purchase.
It said the cost of restructuring was being dealt with in one blow and that things should now start to look better.

"It is clear that the second half will be better in view of the exceptional elements in the first half," Rodocanachi told reporters. "The objective for 1996 is of course to get past the breakeven barrier."
